cataclysmic.mental_hook: The scale of a flood, not of a leak.
cataclysmic.semantic_hint: The adjective for a collapse so total nothing is left standing.

catalyst.required_nuance: starts the change without being consumed by it
catalyst.mental_hook: Starts the reaction. Is not changed by it.
catalyst.semantic_hint: The one event that sets a whole chain of consequences going.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'category' and takes the classifying sense

categorical.mental_hook: No exceptions, no conditions, no maybe.
categorical.semantic_hint: The word for a denial with no qualification of any kind.

incorrect_associations.misconception: keeps the medical sense where emotion is meant

cathartic.required_nuance: release of emotion, never of anything physical
cathartic.mental_hook: A good cry, named by Aristotle.
cathartic.semantic_hint: What a good cry at a sad film is said to be.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the proper noun for the adjective

catholic.required_nuance: breadth of taste, with nothing to do with religion
catholic.mental_hook: Lower case, and about taste rather than faith.
catholic.semantic_hint: The word for a taste in music that takes in absolutely everything.

accepted_concepts: a closed meeting of a faction
a bloc meeting to decide strategy
caucus.mental_hook: The meeting behind the closed door.
caucus.semantic_hint: The closed party meeting where a faction settles its line.

caustic.mental_hook: Burns skin, or burns the person addressed.
caustic.semantic_hint: The word for a remark that burns, and for a chemical that does the same.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the historical noun for the adjective

cavalier.mental_hook: Airy about things that deserve better.
cavalier.semantic_hint: The word for an attitude that treats serious risks as if they were nothing.

cease.mental_hook: Two letters from seize, and the opposite of grabbing.
cease.semantic_hint: What fighting does when a truce is agreed.

cede.required_nuance: formal handing over, usually of territory or rights
cede.mental_hook: Handed over by treaty, not lost in battle.
cede.semantic_hint: What a country does with territory under the terms of a treaty.

celerity.mental_hook: One letter from celebrity, and about speed.
celerity.semantic_hint: The formal word for how quickly an army moves.

censor.mental_hook: One letter from censure, and this one cuts things out.
censor.semantic_hint: What a wartime official does to a soldier's letters home.

accepted_concepts: strong criticism placed on the record
censure.mental_hook: One letter from censor, and this one disapproves.
censure.semantic_hint: The formal vote of disapproval a parliament passes against a minister.

accepted_concepts: a machine that spins to separate substances
a device using spin to divide a mixture
centrifuge.mental_hook: Spins things apart rather than together.
centrifuge.semantic_hint: The laboratory machine that spins a sample until it separates into layers.

cerebral.required_nuance: of the intellect, as against the feelings
cerebral.semantic_hint: The word for a film that engages the head and leaves the heart alone.

chaff.required_nuance: the worthless part, separated from the valuable
chaff.semantic_hint: What you separate from the wheat and throw away.

chagrin.semantic_hint: The sting you feel when you are proved wrong in public.

chamber.required_nuance: an enclosed room, or the body that meets in one
chamber.mental_hook: The room, and the assembly that sits in it.
chamber.semantic_hint: What each of the two houses of a parliament is called.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the noun sense for the verb

champion.mental_hook: The tested sense is the verb: to fight for something.
champion.semantic_hint: What a campaigner does for a cause nobody else will defend.

charlatan.required_nuance: pretends to knowledge they do not have
charlatan.semantic_hint: The word for a doctor with no medical training at all.

chary.mental_hook: Careful about giving, or about committing.
chary.semantic_hint: How someone is with praise when they give it very sparingly.

chastise.semantic_hint: What a headteacher does to a pupil who has gone much too far.

accepted_concepts: excessive loyalty to one's own group

incorrect_associations.misconception: misses the excess that makes it a fault

chauvinism.required_nuance: loyalty pushed until it becomes prejudice
chauvinism.mental_hook: Named for a soldier too devoted to Napoleon.
chauvinism.semantic_hint: The excessive pride in one's own group that shades into contempt for others.

accepted_concepts: someone convinced their own group is superior
a bigot about their own side

incorrect_associations.misconception: misses the excess that makes it a fault

chauvinist.required_nuance: believes their group superior, and says so
chauvinist.mental_hook: Convinced their side is simply better.
chauvinist.semantic_hint: The word for someone convinced their own nation or sex is plainly superior.

accepted_concepts: aggressively convinced of one's group's superiority
prejudiced in favour of one's own

incorrect_associations.misconception: misses the excess and the aggression

chauvinistic.mental_hook: Not proud. Contemptuous of everyone else.
chauvinistic.semantic_hint: The adjective for rhetoric insisting one's own country is simply better than all others.

incorrect_associations.misconception: takes the everyday sense rather than the tested one

check.mental_hook: The tested sense holds something back.
check.semantic_hint: What a dam does to a river, and a rule does to a power.

accepted_concepts: marked by both successes and failures

incorrect_associations.misconception: keeps the literal pattern where a record is meant

checkered.required_nuance: a record with dark squares as well as light
checkered.mental_hook: Light squares and dark ones, in a career.
checkered.semantic_hint: The adjective for a career with as many disgraces as triumphs.

cherish.semantic_hint: What you do with a memory you keep and protect.

chicanery.required_nuance: deception by clever manoeuvre, often legalistic
chicanery.semantic_hint: The clever legal trickery used to get round a rule.

chide.semantic_hint: What a parent does with a mild word rather than a punishment.

accepted_concepts: a fantasy that cannot be realised
chimera.required_nuance: a hope that cannot possibly be fulfilled
chimera.mental_hook: Named for a monster made of mismatched parts.
chimera.semantic_hint: The impossible hope that keeps someone chasing something unattainable.

chivalrous.mental_hook: The knight's code, applied to manners.
chivalrous.semantic_hint: The adjective for the old-fashioned courtesy of a knight's code.

choleric.mental_hook: One of the four humours, and the angry one.
choleric.semantic_hint: The word for a temper that flares at the smallest provocation.

chortle.required_nuance: a gleeful laugh with a snort in it
chortle.mental_hook: Invented by Lewis Carroll, from chuckle and snort.
chortle.semantic_hint: What Lewis Carroll coined from chuckle and snort.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'chronic' and takes duration instead of order

chronological.semantic_hint: How a list is ordered when the earliest event comes first.

churlish.mental_hook: "It would be churlish to refuse" means it would be mean-spirited.
churlish.semantic_hint: The word for refusing a kind offer in an ungracious way.

accepted_concepts: saying in many words what needs few
circumlocution.required_nuance: going round the point rather than at it
circumlocution.mental_hook: Talking round the thing, never at it.
circumlocution.semantic_hint: The long way round a subject that a plain sentence would settle.

circumscribe.mental_hook: A line drawn round it, and nothing outside allowed.
circumscribe.semantic_hint: What a constitution does to the powers of a president.

circumscribed.required_nuance: bounded, with the limits set deliberately
circumscribed.semantic_hint: How a role is described when its powers have been deliberately limited.

incorrect_associations.misconception: hears 'suspect' and reverses who is being wary

circumspect.semantic_hint: How you behave when you weigh every consequence before speaking.
